subject: SIG: audit log export formats + delivery options
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finbank.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: FinBank Security <security@finbank.com>, Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: SIG: audit log export format and delivery options

Hi Rishi,

Were working through the SIG and have a couple of specific asks around audit logs for Redwoods hosted inference service: 1) what event types are captured (auth, API request, model inference, admin changes), 2) canonical schema (column names / example record), 3) retention windows for hosted vs dedicated/private, and 4) delivery/export options (console download, S3, syslog) and whether customers can get automated daily exports.

Can you point us to a sample export and confirm whether logs contain prompt/request payloads or just metadata? FinBanks compliance team needs this to sign off on the SIG.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
FinBank - Security Risk
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finbank.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T11:30:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: audit log export format and delivery options

Hi Elena,

Thanks for the clear list — this is exactly the kind of detail we expect on SIGs. Looping in Monica from Security/Compliance and Laura from Legal for any contract/retention constraints.

Quick answers up front: we capture the core event types you mentioned; we can provide sample exports in NDJSON and Parquet; hosted customers get console export/download while Dedicated/Private customers can configure daily S3 delivery or syslog streaming. Prompt-content storage is controlled (see below). Ill let Monica share the schema and retention nuances.

Would you like the sample export attached in this thread or a secure Drive link? Also happy to schedule a 30-min walkthrough with your compliance team.

Best,
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-14T15:05:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: audit log export format and delivery options

Hi Elena / team,

Thanks for raising these items. Below is a concise summary you can paste into the SIG answers; Ive attached a small sample export (redwood_sample_audit_ndjson.ndjson), a CSV of the schema (log_schema_v1.csv), and a high-level evidence PDF (FinBank_SIG_Evidence_Redwood.pdf).

1) Event types captured (examples):
  - auth.login (user/service authentication attempts, success/failure)
  - api.request (API call metadata: endpoint, model, tokens, latency)
  - inference.result (model completion metadata: status, duration, error codes)
  - admin.change (configuration changes, role/permission updates)
  - billing.usage (aggregated token usage events)

2) Canonical schema (summary):
  - timestamp (RFC3339), event_type, org_id, project_id, request_id, user_id (hashed), source_ip, endpoint, model, tokens_in, tokens_out, duration_ms, status_code, metadata (NDJSON blob for additional structured fields)
  - Full CSV schema attached (log_schema_v1.csv) and sample export (NDJSON).

3) Retention windows (default & options):
  - Hosted (default): 90 days rolling for structured events and metadata.
  - Dedicated: configurable; standard enterprise contracts often specify 365 days.
  - Private (VPC/on-prem): retention is customer-managed; we provide the export/streaming mechanisms.
  - Note: debug-level traces (full request/response bodies) are disabled by default on Hosted. They can be enabled for Dedicated/Private under a contractual agreement and with explicit encryption/KMS controls.

4) Delivery & export options:
  - Console download (ad-hoc CSV/NDJSON) for Hosted
  - Automated daily exports to customer-owned S3 buckets (Dedicated & Private) with server-side encryption using customer KMS key
  - Syslog/HTTPS streaming for near-real-time ingestion (Dedicated only)
  - API-driven on-demand exports (supports date-range queries)

Security & privacy notes:
  - Default Hosted logs do NOT include full unredacted prompt content; we store metadata and deterministic hashes to support correlation.
  - Customers who require full request payload retention must opt in; we then store those logs encrypted at rest and restrict access via RBAC and signed audit trails.
  - All exports are integrity-checked (SHA256) and delivery is logged in our internal audit trail.

If you want, I can: 1) provide a redacted sample showing what a hosted export looks like, 2) open a short security configuration playbook for Dedicated S3 delivery, or 3) schedule a 30-min session to walk your engineers through the schema.

Monica Patel
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
From: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbank.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Elena Ramos <elena.r@finbank.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T08:20:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: audit log export format and delivery options

Thanks Monica — couple of follow ups from our infra team: 1) can you confirm whether request/response bodies (prompts, completions) ever appear in the exported NDJSON for Hosted customers? 2) for the S3 delivery option, will Redwood push objects to a pre-signed path or write directly into our bucket (we prefer write with customer-side KMS control).

Also, does the retained metadata include user-supplied attachments or file names when a customer uploads files to Redwood for processing?

–Tom
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.com>
To: Tom Lee <tom.lee@finbank.com>, Elena Ramos <elena.r@finbank.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-15T10:00:00Z
Subject: Re: SIG: audit log export format and delivery options

Tom — good questions. Short answers below: 1) Hosted NDJSON exports do NOT include full prompt/completion text by default. They include metadata and a deterministic request hash that you can map back to a payload only if you provided us the payload for debugging under an explicit opt-in. 2) For S3 delivery we support direct writes into customer-owned buckets (recommended) using customer KMS key binding; Redwood will request PutObject permissions and write objects directly (not pre-signed uploads). We also support pre-signed delivery where customers prefer to pull files.

Regarding attachments/file names: we store filenames and basic metadata (content type, size) in the event record, but we do not store file contents unless the customer used our file storage APIs to upload — in which case contents follow the same retention and encryption rules as other payloads and are only retained if contractually allowed.

Next steps I propose:
  - Ill drop a redacted NDJSON sample into the Drive link and attach the evidence PDF to this thread (attached).
  - If FinBank wants direct S3 delivery with customer KMS, well raise a Dedicated configuration request (or document the steps for Private deployments).

Laura — from a legal/contract perspective, if FinBank opts to extend Hosted retention or enable full payload logging, do we need an SOW addendum?

Regards,
Monica Patel
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
